objectives: Choose the right form for a power of attorney, depending on the act it serves.
Draft the scope of a power of attorney so that it covers the intended act and nothing more.
Check a power of attorney presented by an agent, including revocation and sub-delegation.
Handle powers of attorney from abroad.
Certify the most common declarations and know the consequences of a false declaration.

cards.front: What form does a power of attorney to sell real estate need?
cards.back: Written, with **signature and content certified at the same time** ([[zzd:37]]).

cards.front: Can a marriage contract or a will be signed through an agent?
What defines the scope of the agent's power towards third parties?
When may an agent sell the principal's property to himself?
A power says it is "irrevocable". May the principal still revoke it?
cards.back: **Yes**: the principal may always revoke; a waiver of that right is invalid ([[zzd:38:2]]).

cards.front: An agent re-delegated his power without authority and without need. Does the sub-agent have power?
cards.back: **No** ([[zzd:43:1]]). An agent who does not inform the principal of a re-delegation answers for the sub-agent's acts as for his own ([[zzd:43:3|Art. 43(3)]]).

cards.front: List the grounds on which a power of attorney ends.
cards.back: Revocation, renunciation, death or judicial disability of either side, end of a legal entity ([[zzd:41:1]]).

cards.front: Does the end of a power affect a third party in good faith?
cards.back: **No**, unless the end was subject to entry and was entered ([[zzd:41:2]]).

cards.front: What does the notary enter in the information system after certifying a revocation?
cards.back: An extract with the parties and the **number and date** of the revoked power and its notary ([[n32:9а::2|Art. 9а item 2 Наредба № 32]]).

cards.front: How can a principal confirm an act made without power?
cards.back: In the **form required for the power** of attorney ([[zzd:42:2]]).

cards.front: What is the fee for the signature on a re-delegation?
A power signed in Germany has only the signature certified by a German notary. Is the form valid?
cards.back: As to form, **yes**: the form of the place of signing is enough ([[kmchp:61]]). For real estate, notaries in practice expect signature and content, an apostille and a translation with the translator's signature certified ([[plzp:21а:1]]).

quiz.question: A client needs a power of attorney to mortgage her flat to a bank. What form?
options: Signature and content certified at the same time
A certified signature only, as for a bank power
Simple written form, signed by the client
A notarial deed of the power of attorney, before a notary
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:37]]: the power follows the form of the deal; when the deal needs a notarial deed, as a mortgage does ([[zzd:167:1]]), the power may be written with signature and content certified at the same time. A bank power concerns operations, not the mortgage itself.

quiz.question: A power says: "to sell my flat in Sofia". The agent wants to donate it to his wife. Is it covered?
options: No; a power to sell does not cover a gift
Yes; a gift is a sale with a price of zero
Yes, if the agent states the gift in the deed
Yes, if the wife accepts the gift in person
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:39:1]]: the scope of the power towards third parties is what the principal stated; a sale and a gift are different deals. A deal that benefits the agent through his wife also calls for the principal's express consent, as self-contracting does ([[zzd:38:1|Art. 38(1)]]).

quiz.question: An agent with a power to sell wants to buy the flat himself. What is needed?
options: The express consent of the principal
Nothing more; the power to sell is enough
The permission of the district court
The consent of the notary, in the deed
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:38:1]]: the agent may not contract in the name of the principal with himself, or with another person he also represents, unless the principal consented. The consent comes from the principal, not from a court or the notary.

quiz.question: A power of attorney says it is "irrevocable". What is the legal position?
options: The principal can still revoke it; the waiver is invalid
It cannot be revoked; the principal waived the right
It can be revoked only by a court, on a claim of the principal
It can be revoked only after one year, by a notice
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:38:2]]: the principal may always revoke the power and the agent may always renounce it; a waiver of that right by either side is invalid. The word "irrevocable" has no effect.

quiz.question: The principal died last week. The agent comes to sign a sale under the power. What does the office do?
options: Refuses; the power ended with the death
Proceeds, if the agent did not know of the death
Proceeds, if the heirs agree to the sale orally
Proceeds, if the power was certified by a notary
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:41:1]]: the power ends with the death of the principal. The heirs may sell themselves, or give a new power; an oral consent is not a power.

quiz.question: An agent re-delegated his power to a friend, although the power does not allow it, and nothing urgent required it. What is the position?
options: The re-delegation is not allowed; the friend has no power
It is valid, because the agent trusts the friend
It is valid, if the re-delegation is certified by a notary
It is valid for movables, but not for real estate
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:43:1]]: an agent may re-delegate only when authorised, or when the re-delegation became necessary to protect the interests of the principal. A certification does not create a power that the agent could not give.

quiz.question: What must the office do right after certifying the revocation of a power to sell real estate?
options: Enter an extract with the number and date of the revoked power
Nothing; the revocation takes effect with the certification
Send the revocation to the agent by registered letter with a receipt
Destroy the copy of the old power in the office's file
quiz.explanation: [[n32:9а::2|Art. 9а item 2 of Ordinance No. 32]]: after certifying a document that revokes a power, the notary enters and sends at once to the information system an extract with the data of the parties, the number and date of the revoked power and the name and number of the notary who certified it.

quiz.question: A person sold a flat as "agent" without a power. Can the owner make the sale valid?
options: Yes, by confirming it in the form required for the power
No; a sale without power is null and cannot be confirmed
Yes, orally before the notary who issued the deed
Yes, by a simple letter to the buyer and the notary
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:42:2]]: the person in whose name a contract was concluded without power may confirm it, in the form required for the power to conclude that contract: for a sale of real estate, signature and content certified at the same time ([[zzd:37|Art. 37]]).

quiz.question: A Bulgarian in Canada needs to sell a flat in Plovdiv. Which is a valid route?
options: A Canadian notary certifies the power, with an apostille and a translation
A scan of a letter signed by the client, sent by e-mail to the office
A video call with the Bulgarian notary, recorded and filed by the office staff
A power signed before an officer of a Canadian bank, with a translation
quiz.explanation: [[kmchp:61]]: the form of the place of signing is enough. For real estate, Bulgarian notaries in practice expect a certification of the signature and the content, an apostille and a translation into Bulgarian with the translator's signature certified ([[plzp:21а:1]]). A bank officer is not a certifying authority.

quiz.question: The principal revoked a bank power on Monday. On Tuesday the agent withdrew money; the bank knew nothing of the revocation. Is the bank protected?
options: Yes; the end of the power cannot be opposed to a bank in good faith
No; the revocation acts against everyone from its certification
No; the extract in the Chamber's system binds the bank from Monday morning
Yes, but only if the agent returns the money to the principal
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:41:2]]: the end of a power cannot be opposed to third persons who contracted with the agent in good faith, unless the end was subject to entry and was entered. The extract in the Chamber's system serves the notaries' checks; it is not such an entry. The principal informs the bank and claims from the agent.

quiz.question: What does a notarial certification of a signature on a declaration prove?
options: Who signed the declaration, and when
That the facts in the declaration are true
That the declarant has no public debts
That the declarant will keep the promise
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:589:2]]: the notary certifies that the person signed, or confirmed the signature, before the notary on that date. [[gpk:180]]: a private document proves that its statements were made by the signatory, not that they are true; a false declaration is a crime (Art. 313 НК).

quiz.question: A power of attorney names two agents and says nothing about how they act. May one of them sign the sale alone?
options: Yes; each may act alone, unless the power says otherwise
No; both must sign together in every case
No; the principal must first choose one of them
Yes, but only with the written consent of the other agent
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:39:2]]: when several persons are authorised for an act, each of them may perform it alone, unless the authorisation shows otherwise. A principal who wants joint action writes it in the power.
